scope: Independent read-only review of final early-case shortcut and actual final-header exhaustive rerun. Final numerical performance review and full validation are separate.
findings: The direct static assertion preserves the signed integral <=64-bit type contract on every branch; algorithm/cstdint/type_traits facilities now have direct includes.
The N<=INT_MAX assertion executes first. Short-circuit evaluation of N<=2 prevents evaluation of begin()+1 or points[0] on an empty vector.
Every early-return path loops over all coordinates with the original wide debug assertions; nonuniform inputs retain convex_hull validation before geometry.
N<2 returns {-1,-1}; N=2 or all-equal N>=3 returns {0,1}, normalized and distinct regardless of coordinate equality.
Leaving the shortcut implies N>=3 and at least two distinct coordinates. Therefore H>=2 and removing the old H==1 return is sound.
All remaining hull/caliper/index-recovery code is unchanged. The existing exact-arithmetic, antipodal-coverage and <2H support-advance proof applies.

All-equal detection may add a real O(N) scan on a long equal prefix followed by a differing point. Full worst-case O(N log(N+1))/O(N) bounds are unchanged; fast returns are O(1) auxiliary space, O(1) time for N<=2 and O(N) time for larger all-equal inputs.
API documentation at recorded hash accurately describes shortcut complexity, validation, added scan, ownership, type and tie semantics; no timing claims added.
limits: One authorized sequential GCC14 build/run, not a repeated compiler matrix or performance sample.

The same independent int256 oracle harness source was copied unchanged to the new namespace; it covers all two-grid 4x4 subsets, reordered/duplicated inputs and scaled signed-permutation trap subsets.
Production header/test/docs were not modified by this reviewer. Full validation, negative contract probes and performance evidence are owned separately.
